Text is read from the app through the accessibility service: it is exact, available immediately and needs no network. This works only in apps that report character positions to accessibility services; in other apps and for text in images, the screen is recognized as usual.\n\nExperimental: some apps report incorrect character positions, which shifts the highlight or selects a neighboring word. In that case, turn the option off.
No screenshots and no recognition. Text in images is not read.

Screen recognition is off: only text that apps provide to accessibility services is read. Text in images, manga, games and apps that do not provide their text is not read.\n\nIntended for e-ink readers, older or low-end devices where recognition is unavailable or slow, and for slow or metered connections: no battery is spent on recognition and no data is sent.

Sends parts of the screen to cloud recognition separately, at a higher resolution relative to the whole screenshot, so that small text missed by a full-screen scan is recognized. Turn on only if small text is not recognized: each part is an extra request and uses more data.

On demand: the part under the aim, when the aim stays on an area where nothing was found.

Always: the whole screen in parts with every scan (more data).
Recommended: Both. Turn one engine off only on low-end or heavily loaded devices. Cloud recognition uses mobile data (about 0.1–0.4 MB per scan); on-device recognition does not.

Both: on-device and cloud recognition start at the same time. On-device recognition reads the text around the aim first, so words are available almost immediately; the more accurate cloud result replaces it when it arrives. Without a network connection or on a cloud error, the on-device result is kept.

Cloud: nothing is recognized without a network connection; words are available only after the server responds.

Device: works offline, but recognizes vertical text and manga less accurately; OCR boost is unavailable.

On-device recognition of the whole screen starts only if cloud recognition has not responded within 3 s. Reduces load and battery use; words away from the aim become available later. Keep off when speed matters more.

A free online service translates the sentence around the word. The translation is machine-made and may be inaccurate, and the sentence is sent to the service’s server.

The services are used without an account: Bing (the Microsoft Translator website), Google Translate and the translator built into Microsoft Edge. They do not publish their limits; when a service rejects a request, the next one is used. The first Bing request in an hour takes about a second longer because a key is loaded from the Bing website first.

The first enabled service translates the sentence. If it returns an error or does not respond within 3 seconds, the next one is used. Drag the handle to change the order.

Keep the system from stopping the bubble
The system restarts the bubble\'s service on its own, unless one of these settings stops it to save power. Both are the system\'s own settings: Screenlate only opens them.

Find Screenlate in the list and turn optimization off for it (“Don’t optimize”, “Unrestricted” or similar). If Screenlate is not listed, check “All apps”.

Screenlate uses its accessibility service to show the bubble over other apps and to read the text under it.

• A screenshot, when you tap the bubble or pull it out. With App text only, only for a picture in an Anki note.\n• The text apps show on the screen, at the same moments, when Read app text or App text only is on.\n• Which app is open and where the keyboard and the system bars are: to hide the bubble in the apps you chose and to keep it off the bars.

• The screenshot goes to cloud text recognition, unless Engines is set to Device or App text only is on. On-device recognition sends nothing.
• The sentence goes to an online translator when you tap the translation button or a note template asks for its translation.
• The word and its reading go to the audio sources you chose, for the pronunciation.
• Notes go to AnkiDroid on this device.

The service does not tap or type anything for you. What it reads is not saved: the screenshot stays in memory only until the bubble is docked again, a note gets only the part of the screenshot you select, and the logs never hold text from the screen.
